cards.explanation: The answer is Spirit. Luke says Jesus was "…led by the Spirit into the wilderness…" (Luke 4:1). He didn't wander out there by accident or because He lost the map. The same verse says He was full of the Holy Spirit when it happened.

The answer is True. Luke says Jesus "…ate nothing during those days, and when they had ended, He was hungry." (Luke 4:2). Plain as day, friends. Forty days with no food, and I'd be hungry by the second one.

The answer is bread. The devil says, "If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread." (Luke 4:3). Jesus had eaten nothing for forty days, so bread was right where the dare landed. I'll be honest, friends, a stone is a rough place to start baking.

The answer is that He quotes what is written. Jesus answers, "It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’" (Luke 4:4). He answers with the written Word. That's a good reminder for all of us who get hungry and want to give in.

The answer is True. The devil says, "I will give You authority over all these kingdoms and all their glory…" (Luke 4:6). He's showing Jesus every kingdom of the world and offering the whole lot. That's a big offer, friends, and I can't even offer you a whole batch without eating two.

The answer is that Jesus has to worship him. The devil says, "So if You worship me, it will all be Yours." (Luke 4:7). There's the catch, bakers. Every offer has a price tag, and the price he names is worship.

The answer is the Lord your God only. Jesus answers, "It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’" (Luke 4:8). Worship and service both go to the Lord your God, bakers. That's His answer to the offer.

The answer is Scripture. The devil says, "For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully…" (Luke 4:10). Yes, friends, he quotes the Bible. It's a good reminder that a verse can be quoted and still be pointed the wrong way.

The answer is to put the Lord your God to the test. Jesus answers, "It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’" (Luke 4:12). Notice the word "also," friends. Jesus isn't throwing out the devil's verse, He's setting another one beside it.

The answer is False. Luke says, "When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Him until an opportune time." (Luke 4:13). That "until" matters, bakers. He left for a while, and the text never says he's gone for good.
